items.title: Hal Galper interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 27, 2022
items.q: And Tony [Marino], Tony has, I’ve been playing with Tony for decades.

ctx.x: Not good. It doesn’t look good. You’ve got to get it memorized. And Tony [Marino], Tony has, I’ve been playing with Tony for decades. He’s a consum — he’s a symphony master bassist. It doesn’t make any — I can get lost and he’ll just follow me. It doesn’t make any difference to him or to me, whichever way we go Tony is going to be there. It just never fails. He’ll just go — like I said I have a short term memory problem. Sometimes, like this Saturday we were playing a song and I got distracted and I totally lost…
I wonder if they’re thinking how are we going to get out of this now. How is this going to resolve itself.

items.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025
items.q: Galper talked about that too, Hal Galper, when I play with him about the big beat.

ctx.x: Yeah a lot of guys are that way. I like to be in the middle for sure, between whatever the chordal instrument is and the drums, and I don’t have to be on the hi-hat side. When I’m locking in my time, I’m listening to what the right hand or – not everybody is a right handed drummer – but the time. Where the quarter note is coming from if we’re playing swing and jazz. You know? I want to know – that’s where I get the time from, his hands,

more than that hi-hat two and four. You know. So I’m listening for that. And that lets me know if I’m in sync with his quarter note, if I’m a little behind I’m a little bit – and every drummer’s different. You know I play with guys that really are on top of the beat and you’ve really gotta push. And then you get used to playing with a guy like that, then you’re playing with someone that plays a little behind the beat and you’re pushing him and you don’t want to push him. You know? You want to relax and breathe.…

I remember hearing Louis Hayes and I think it was Ron Carter on bass at the Iridium. This was quite a few years ago. And Louis Hayes was so on top of the beat that I couldn’t understand how the song did not speed up like significantly. How is that possible? Man he just like constant push yet not speeding up I guess.
